\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{خوف} (khauf)}{خوف (khauf)}]{\ur{خوف} (khauf) — dread; fear}

\label{lesson:UR-C445-khauf}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for displeased, then the Urdu for a fit of rage.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{خوف}}
\textbf{\ur{خوف}} — \emph{khauf} — \textquotedblleft{}dread; fear\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{جنگل} \ur{میں} \ur{رات} \ur{کو} \ur{خوف} \ur{لگتا} \ur{ہے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jangal meṅ rāt ko khauf lagtā hai.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the forest at night you feel a sense of dread.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{خوف}} (\emph{khauf}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{khawf}, \textquotedblleft{}fear\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khauf}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{khauf}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jangal meṅ rāt ko khauf lagtā hai.} — In the forest at night you feel a sense of dread.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for displeased, then the Urdu for a fit of rage, then say \emph{khauf} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{خوف} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Dread; fear\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{ڈرانا} (ḍarānā)}{ڈرانا (ḍarānā)}]{\ur{ڈرانا} (ḍarānā) — to frighten}

\label{lesson:UR-C445-darana}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a fit of rage, then the Urdu for dread.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{ڈرانا}}
\textbf{\ur{ڈرانا}} — \emph{ḍarānā} — \textquotedblleft{}to frighten\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بلی} \ur{نے} \ur{چوہے} \ur{کو} \ur{ڈرایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{billī ne chūhe ko ḍarāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The cat frightened the mouse.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{بچوں} \ur{کو} \ur{ڈرایا}, \emph{us ne bachchoṅ ko ḍarāyā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{ڈرانا}} (\emph{ḍarānā}) is the causative of \emph{ḍarnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be afraid\textquotedblright{}, inherited from Sanskrit \emph{darati}, \textquotedblleft{}is frightened\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 6190); the noun \textbf{\ur{ڈر}}, \textquotedblleft{}fear\textquotedblright{}, belongs to the same word.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍarānā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ḍarānā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{billī ne chūhe ko ḍarāyā.} — The cat frightened the mouse.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a fit of rage, then the Urdu for dread, then say \emph{ḍarānā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{ڈرانا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To frighten\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سہمنا} (sahamnā)}{سہمنا (sahamnā)}]{\ur{سہمنا} (sahamnā) — to cower (in fright)}

\label{lesson:UR-C445-sahamna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for dread, then the Urdu for to frighten.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سہمنا}}
\textbf{\ur{سہمنا}} — \emph{sahamnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to cower (in fright)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{کتے} \ur{کو} \ur{دیکھ} \ur{کر} \ur{لڑکی} \ur{سہم} \ur{گئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{kutte ko dekh kar laṛkī saham gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The girl cowered when she saw the dog.
\end{quote}

Past (she …): \ur{وہ} \ur{سہم} \ur{گئی}, \emph{voh saham gaī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سہمنا}} (\emph{sahamnā}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{sahm}, \textquotedblleft{}fear, dread\textquotedblright{}, made into an Urdu verb with \emph{-nā}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sahamnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kutte ko dekh kar laṛkī saham gaī.} — The girl cowered when she saw the dog.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for dread, then the Urdu for to frighten, then say \emph{sahamnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{دبکنا} (dubaknā)}{دبکنا (dubaknā)}]{\ur{دبکنا} (dubaknā) — to crouch out of sight}

\label{lesson:UR-C445-dubakna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to frighten, then the Urdu for to cower.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{دبکنا}}
\textbf{\ur{دبکنا}} — \emph{dubaknā} — \textquotedblleft{}to crouch out of sight\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بلی} \ur{ڈر} \ur{کر} \ur{کرسی} \ur{کے} \ur{نیچے} \ur{دبک} \ur{گئی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{billī ḍar kar kursī ke nīche dubak gaī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The cat took fright and crouched under the chair.
\end{quote}

Past (he …): \ur{وہ} \ur{دبک} \ur{گیا}, \emph{voh dubak gayā}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{دبکنا}} (\emph{dubaknā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{dabaknā}, \textquotedblleft{}to be hidden\textquotedblright{}, under \emph{dabb}, \textquotedblleft{}press\textquotedblright{}, a form it reconstructs (CDIAL 6173).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dubaknā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{dubaknā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{billī ḍar kar kursī ke nīche dubak gaī.} — The cat took fright and crouched under the chair.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to frighten, then the Urdu for to cower, then say \emph{dubaknā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{دبکنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To crouch out of sight\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{سمٹنا} (simaṭnā)}{سمٹنا (simaṭnā)}]{\ur{سمٹنا} (simaṭnā) — to huddle; to shrink into oneself}

\label{lesson:UR-C445-simatna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to cower, then the Urdu for to crouch out of sight.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{سمٹنا}}
\textbf{\ur{سمٹنا}} — \emph{simaṭnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to huddle; to shrink into oneself\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سردی} \ur{میں} \ur{بچے} \ur{کمبل} \ur{میں} \ur{سمٹ} \ur{گئے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sardī meṅ bachche kambal meṅ simaṭ gae.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
In the cold the children huddled under the blanket.
\end{quote}

Past (she …): \ur{وہ} \ur{کونے} \ur{میں} \ur{سمٹ} \ur{گئی}, \emph{voh kone meṅ simaṭ gaī}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{سمٹنا}} (\emph{simaṭnā}) is inherited: CDIAL lists the Hindi cousin \emph{simaṭnā}, \textquotedblleft{}to shrink, to be gathered in\textquotedblright{}, under Sanskrit \emph{saṃvēṣṭayati}, \textquotedblleft{}wraps up\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 13026).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for describing what you lived and felt.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{simaṭnā}, once more

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for to cower, then the Urdu for to crouch out of sight, then say \emph{simaṭnā} again
\end{itemize}
